newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss publish detailed reply to WW2 gold report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss publish detailed reply to WW2 gold report.

text.p: Switzerland on Thursday issued a detailed response to a U.S. report on its World War Two gold dealings in which it again said the Allies had all the facts in 1946 when they negotiated an accord over gold bought from Germany.

"At the conclusion of the Washington Agreement in 1946 the parties to the signing realised all essential facts. Thanks to their intelligence sources, the Allies even had precise knowledge of the Swiss negotiating position," the Swiss cabinet said in its official response to the report.

The Swiss statement follows the release of a report in Washington on May 7 in which U.S. undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat and the State Department's chief historian criticised both the U.S. and Switzerland for their handling of Nazi gold after the war.
The report also concluded that some of the gold the Nazis took from individual Holocaust victims was melted down and sold to Switzerland along with gold the Nazis looted from occupied countries.
At that time the Swiss cabinet issued a brief response to the Eizenstat commission's findings and it reiterated its view that there was no grounds for discussing the reopening the 1946 gold accord.

In today's report the Swiss cabinet said it had reservations about the foreword of the Eizenstat report, which contained "political and moral values which go beyond the historic report" and which in the Swiss government's opinion require clarification.

Switzerland in 1946 agreed to give the Allies 250 million Swiss francs worth of gold as a voluntary contribution toward the reconstruction of Europe. In return, the Allies agreed to drop any future claims on Switzerland over the gold deals.

The report, published by the Swiss cabinet, also took issue with criticism of Swiss neutrality, although it conceded that in hindsight, Switzerland knows that its neutral stance during the war led to mistakes.
